ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The principle of power generation in an alternator is that a rectangular coil rotates uniformly around an axis \( O O^{\prime} \) perpendicular to the magnetic field in a uniform magnetic field. A small generator has a coil with a total of 220 turns, a coil area \( S = 0.05 \, \mathrm{m}^{2} \), a coil rotation frequency of \( 50 \, \mathrm{Hz} \), negligible internal resistance, and a magnetic field strength \( B = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\pi} \) (T). To use the alternating current generated by this generator to power two motors labeled "220V, 11kW" normally, an ideal transformer needs to be connected between the generator's output terminals \( a, b \) and the motors, as shown in the circuit diagram.

1. What is the turns ratio of the primary and secondary coils of the transformer?
2. What is the reading of the AC ammeter connected in series with the primary coil of the transformer?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The principle of power generation in an alternator is that a rectangular coil rotates uniformly around an axis \( O O^{\prime} \) perpendicular to the magnetic field in a uniform magnetic field. A small generator has a coil with a total of 220 turns, a coil area \( S = 0.05 \, \mathrm{m}^{2} \), a coil rotation frequency of \( 50 \, \mathrm{Hz} \), negligible internal resistance, and a magnetic field strength \( B = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{\pi} \) (T). To use the alternating current generated by this generator to power two motors labeled "220V, 11kW" normally, an ideal transformer needs to be connected between the generator's output terminals \( a, b \) and the motors, as shown in the circuit diagram. 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is a rectangular-coil generator. The coil rotates around the vertical dashed axis OO′, and the direction of the magnetic field B is indicated by a horizontal arrow pointing to the right. The two output terminals of the coil are labeled a and b, and are connected to the primary-coil circuit of the transformer on the right; the AC ammeter A is connected in series in the primary-coil circuit of the transformer. The secondary coil of the transformer is connected to two motors M1 and M2; in the figure, the two motors are connected in parallel across the two ends of the secondary coil. Then reason: The total number of turns of the generator coil is N=220, the area is S=0.05 m^2, the rotational frequency is f=50 Hz, the angular velocity is ω=2πf=100π rad/s, and the magnetic induction intensity is B=2√2/π T. The maximum value of the induced electromotive force produced by the rotation of the coil is E_m=NBSω=220×(2√2/π)×0.05×100π=2200√2 V. The effective value of the AC voltage is U_p=E_m/√2=2200 V. The internal resistance of the generator is ignored, so the voltage across the primary coil of the transformer is 2200 V. The two motors are both marked “220V, 11kW”, and in the figure they are connected in parallel across the two ends of the transformer secondary coil, so the secondary-coil voltage should be U_s=220 V. An ideal transformer satisfies N_p/N_s=U_p/U_s=2200/220=10/1. When the two motors work normally, the total power is P=2×11 kW=22 kW. For an ideal transformer, the input power equals the output power, so the input power of the primary coil is also 22 kW. The effective value of the primary-coil current is I_p=P/U_p=22000 W / 2200 V=10 A. Therefore, the reading of the AC ammeter connected in series in the primary coil is 10 A.
